title: Variance-slice benchmark: AWQ vs GPTQ jitter scan (Nov 2026)
summary: Experiment notebook for a 'variance-slice' technique: partitioning inference traffic by per-request activation variance and scanning AWQ vs GPTQ quantized kernels across INT8/FP8. Focus: tail latency under jittered microbatch arrival patterns and quality regressions on stress prompts.
content:
Goal and motivation:
- Problem: standard throughput/avg-latency benching masks cases where quantization noise amplifies on high-activation-variance requests, causing surprising quality dips and kernel-induced stalls.
- Approach: create a small bench and profiling harness that slices requests by a simple pre-eval statistic (per-token activation variance computed on first 16 tokens) and runs AWQ and GPTQ variants in parallel traces to expose differential failure modes.

Hypothesis:
1) AWQ will show lower average cost but higher variance-induced quality regressions on the top 10% activation-variance slice.
2) GPTQ (layerwise per-channel quant) will be more robust on long-context low-entropy workloads but incur higher P99 latency due to kernel tiling inefficiencies on our current fused GEMM path.

Harness and workload details:
- Models: r-infer/gpt-7b-v0 (FP32 baseline), r-infer/gpt-7b-awq-int8, r-infer/gpt-7b-gptq-int8, and r-infer/gpt-7b-fp8-proxy (same weights cast to fp8 emulation).
- Kernel implementations: fused-gemm (baseline), vector-lane-fused (our experimental simd path), mmap-packed (memory-packed path for int8).
- Traffic generation: mixed mix of 100K synthetic prompts derived from three corpora: conversational, knowledge/QA, and code completion seeds. Each prompt appended with adversarial tail triggers (long repetitive tokens, punctuation-heavy sequences) for stress.
- Slice metric: compute activation variance over first 16 output tokens using a lightweight prefix run on FP32 compiled to a single forward pass; label each request as low/med/high variance (quantiles 0-60, 60-90, 90-100).
- Arrival patterns: steady (50 qps), bursty (Poisson bursts up to 500 qps), jittered microbatches (random microbatching with jitter ±20ms).
- Measurements: avg latency, P95, P99, P99.9, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU occupancy, kernel switch counts, mismatch rate (where quantized output differs from FP32 baseline beyond threshold), perplexity delta, and a simple semantic-similarity delta (embedding cosine with FP32 baseline).

Profiling knobs and tracer configuration:
- Use our microprof shim to trace: NVTX spans, kernel name, occupancy, and memory-bound flags.
- Enable KV-cache warmup traces with warmup length 256 for half of the runs.
- Add deterministic RNG seeds for AWQ stochastic steps to replay jitter experiments.

Key findings (early/draft numbers):
- High-variance slice (top 10%): AWQ-int8 shows a mismatch rate of ~7.3% vs FP32; GPTQ-int8 shows ~2.1%. For low-variance slice: AWQ-int8 ~0.8%, GPTQ-int8 ~0.6%.
- Latency: on bursty arrival + jittered microbatches, fused-gemm + AWQ-int8 median latency = 28 ms/token, P99 = 120 ms/token; GPTQ-int8 on mmap-packed median = 33 ms/token, P99 = 240 ms/token (we saw kernel-switch stalls where mmap packing caused longer blocking).
- FP8-proxy variant shows similar avg-latency to AWQ-int8 but slightly higher mismatch rate on knowledge-QA prompts (mismatch ~1.9%).
- Kernel behavior: vector-lane-fused decreased P99 by ~20% on long-context runs but increased avg GPU memory churn; memory profiler shows increased page-writes in mmap-packed when activation variance high (correlates with stalls).
- Quality/perp: perplexity delta (quant - FP32) on high-variance slice: AWQ-int8 +3.5 ppl, GPTQ-int8 +0.9 ppl. Semantic-similarity (embedding cosine): AWQ median 0.84 vs GPTQ 0.92 on high-variance prompts.

Reproducibility notes:
- Seeds and config files stored under the bench-run folder in infra (see linked artifacts).
- Small cross-check script used to replay exact traces: scripts/variance_replay.sh (PR linked above).
- Timing: warmup traces and microbatch jitter combine to produce non-linear stalls; to reproduce, ensure jitter seed=20261115 and microbatch window=12ms in runtime config.

Hypothesis-driven analysis (work-in-progress):
- Mechanism: AWQ scales quantization noise with activation magnitude; high-variance sequences amplify noise per-token causing decoder drift which then triggers longer generation paths and higher kernel switching frequency.
- Stalls: mmap-packed kernel path interacts poorly with our allocator under jittered microbatches; page-churn and kernel-request serialization lead to long tail.

Immediate next steps / experiments to run:
- Run A/B with AWQ with tightened per-layer clipping (reduce outlier sensitivity) and measure mismatch delta on the top 10% slice.
- Sweep vector-lane-fused tile size (4/8/16) to see if we can recover median latency without the extra memory churn.
- Re-run mmap-packed with a larger prefetch window to reduce page-writes during high-variance bursts.
- Add human-eval spot-checks (5 raters) on 200 high-variance prompts comparing outputs from AWQ and GPTQ for hallucination/correctness.

Action items and ownership:
- Mateo: run AWQ per-layer clipping sweep (deadline 2026-11-23).
- Priya: instrument allocator traces for mmap path and produce waterfall for page-writes (deadline 2026-11-20).
- Luca: run vector-lane tile sweep and submit microbench results (deadline 2026-11-22).
- Anika (me): consolidate replay scripts and update bench README with exact flags (in progress).

Open questions / risks:
- Are the observed mismatches true output regressions or just surface differences (e.g., synonyms)? Need human rater checks.
- Is mmap-packed salvageable with allocator tweaks or is the design fundamentally incompatible with jittered microbatch arrivals at high qps?
- Does FP8 reliably offer a middle ground for both quality and latency under these slices, or are there corner cases that break it badly?

Appendix (short):
- Quick command used for a single run: 
  ./bench_run --model r-infer/gpt-7b-awq-int8 --kernel fused-gemm --traffic mix.json --slice-method variance16 --jitter-seed 20261115 --out results/awq-variance-20261115.json
- Small table (draft numbers):
  ModelVariant, Slice, Median(ms/token), P99(ms/token), MismatchRate(%)
  AWQ-int8, High, 30, 120, 7.3
  GPTQ-int8, High, 35, 240, 2.1
  AWQ-int8, Low, 26, 65, 0.8
  GPTQ-int8, Low, 28, 72, 0.6

Notes: this is a working doc intended to capture an exploration pattern (variance-slicing + jitter scanning). If the hypothesis holds, we should add a 'slice-aware routing' idea to our runtime: route high-variance requests to more robust quant kernels (e.g., GPTQ or fp8) by default.

If you want raw traces or the perf CSV exports, say which run id and I will drop them in the shared bench artifact folder.
